literal: 1 From Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through styled Central Capital Xiande Prefecture: "originally Chaoxian territory"—according to Shiji 115 Chaoxian Traditions and Hanshu 28b Geographic Treatise, it should read "originally Yan state territory."
idiomatic: First note: from Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through "Central Capital Xiande Prefecture," the phrase "originally Chaoxian territory" should, per Shiji 115 and Hanshu 28b, read "originally Yan state territory."

literal: This section wrongly takes Liaoyang for Pyongyang.
idiomatic: This section wrongly identifies Liaoyang with Pyongyang.

literal: Moreover, according to New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture—not Pyongyang, and not Liaoyang.
idiomatic: Per New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture, not Pyongyang or Liaoyang.

literal: 2 From Taizu founding the state and attacking Bohai through seizing Hohan city to Shence year 4 repairing Liaoyang old walls and building Dongping Commandery as defense prefecture: repairing Liaoyang and building Dongping come first; attacking Bohai and seizing Hohan come after—the narrative order is inverted.
idiomatic: Second note: repairing Liaoyang and founding Dongping precede the Bohai campaign and seizure of Hohan—the sequence is inverted.

literal: It is suspected that "formerly" two characters were lost before Shence year 4.
idiomatic: Likely "formerly" was lost before Shence year 4.

literal: 3 City named Tianfu: according to the Annals, Tianxian year 1 second month changed Hohan city to Tianfu.
idiomatic: Third note: "city named Tianfu"—the Annals place the Hohan-to-Tianfu rename in Tianxian year 1, month 2.

literal: It was not when Dongping was raised to Nanjing that Dongping was called Tianfu.
idiomatic: Tianfu was not the name given when Dongping became Nanjing.

literal: 4 Governing eighty-seven prefectures, fu, armies, and cities: the figure "eighty-seven" does not match the list of prefectures, fu, armies, and cities below.
idiomatic: Fourth note: "eighty-seven" prefectures, fu, armies, and cities does not match the list below.

literal: 5 "Originally Han Loufang County land": Loufang—in Hanshu Geographic Treatise and Hou Hanshu Commanderies and States both write Loufang, belonging to Lelang Commandery.
idiomatic: Fifth note: "Loufang County"—Hanshu and Hou Hanshu both have Loufang in Lelang Commandery.

literal: 6 "Shengzong returned from campaigning Goryeo": the original erroneously read "Silla"; corrected per Annals Tonghe year 3 seventh month and year 10 first month.
idiomatic: Sixth note: "Goryeo" was written "Silla" in the original; corrected from Annals Tonghe 3.7 and 10.1.

literal: 7 "At the end of Tonghe Goryeo surrendered"—the six characters "at the end of Tonghe, Goryeo surrendered" were wrongly placed after "Kaitai year 3 took its Bao and Ding two prefectures," reversing chronology; now corrected.
idiomatic: Seventh note: "at Tonghe's end Goryeo surrendered" was misplaced after the Kaitai seizure of Bao and Ding—now reordered.

literal: 8 Heduan: Daoguang Hall edition Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia as Herui.
idiomatic: Eighth note: Heduan—Daoguang Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia's Herui.

literal: 9 "Bohai established the prefecture"—the four characters "Bohai established the prefecture" were originally missing; Daoguang Hall edition added them per Tongkao.
idiomatic: Ninth note: "Bohai established the prefecture" was missing; Daoguang edition restored it from Tongkao.

literal: The present text follows that.
idiomatic: The present text follows that addition.
